newsitem.title: CHILE: Severe weather hits ports, towns in central Chile.
newsitem.headline: Severe weather hits ports, towns in central Chile.

text.p: Five of Chile's largest ports remained closed on Sunday as severe storms caused flash floods and mudslides in the country's central region, the Chilean Office of National Emergencies (ONEMI) said.
The ports of Valparaiso, San Antonio, Quinteros, Talcahuano and Lirquen were closed late Saturday and may remain so until Tuesday, when the weather is forecast to improve, an ONEMI official said.
The storms have not hit the northern ports that serve Chile's biggest copper mines, the official said.
The downpour, however, disrupted the long weekend for hundreds of thousands of holidaymakers and residents in the central region.
One woman was reported missing after the car she was travelling in fell in a rain-swollen pond near the coastal city of Coquimbo, the local Radio Cooperativa said.
Rescue workers had to evacuate some 122 people from their flooded homes across the central region, while in Valparaiso at least four houses were hit by mudslides.
Up in the Andes mountains, heavy snow storms led to the closing of two border crossings to Argentina: Jama in the north and Los Libertadores in the central region.

The storm dumped 52 millimeters (two inches) of rain over the past 24 hours in metropolitan Santiago, the government-run weather service said, roughly one-sixth of the precipitation expected in a normal year.
